items.text: “Last week we walked PROAPT — a six-step practice for hearing God in scripture.”
“One sentence about how that practice has been?”
A parent starts — arranged beforehand, never a cold call on a teen
Two or three voluntary contributions; anyone may pass — kept brief, tonight’s arc needs the time
Two passages, read slowly — Psalm 23 and John 15:1–11 — “Listen as if you have not heard it.”
Scripture pictures the heart as cultivated ground — green pastures, still waters, vine and vinedresser
Tonight we walk into that image: picture your heart as a garden, invite Jesus in, notice what He does
Imaginative prayer — Ignatius taught it, Bonaventure taught it, the Puritan writers under other names
Not visualization-as-self-help, not contemplative emptying — filling the mind with one scriptural image
“The exercise is not a test of imaginative power. It is a posture of receptivity.”

panel.label: JOHN 15:5
lines: “I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.”

items.text: We stay right here, together, as one room — a guided imaginative prayer, twelve to fifteen minutes, read slowly
Eyes closed or open — either is fine; your own family is beside you the whole time
Then five minutes with your journal, then family clusters for sharing — by invitation only
A parent will open each round — “Silence is a complete answer.”
“Father, you are the vinedresser. … Where it is hard, be tender. Where it is closed, be patient. Where it is opening, be present.”

slides.title: The Garden Exercise — Whole Room, then Clusters

items.text: Settle (2 min) — “Take a breath. Settle. Eyes open or closed. Whatever feels honest. We have time.”
Guided prayer (12–15 min) — read slowly to the whole room; the pauses are not optional — they are where the work happens
Silent journaling (5 min) — “Write in your Week 9 journal page what you noticed. Whatever you noticed.”
Sharing in family clusters (8–10 min) — by invitation only; a parent opens; silence is a complete answer
Receive without interpreting — “Thank you for sharing that.” Never “God was telling you _____.”
If something painful surfaces — bless it: “I hear that. May Jesus stay with you in that place this week.”
“What happened in your cluster stays in your cluster.”
One word about tonight — not what was said, but what you noticed
“Surprised.” “Tender.” “Empty.” “Found.” “Confused.” “Quiet.”
A parent begins; anyone may pass — each word received without commentary
“Whatever happened tonight is yours. Some of it will keep happening across the week.”
Three returns to the garden this week — five to ten minutes each, journaled
“You don’t need the full guided script — you have the place now. Just go back.”
Notice what is the same and what has changed — notice if Jesus is in a different place than He was tonight
Pick three days and a time — morning before the day starts is often best
If something heavy surfaces — stop, open your eyes, come back another day; tell a trusted adult
Came in skeptical? The Note for the Skeptic handout is for you — adapting or sitting out for now is okay
